chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassaan, from Musa ibn Bakr who said:

A boy complained to Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him), so he asked about him, and they told him that he had spleen trouble. So he said: 'Feed him leek for three days.' So we fed it to him, the blood was expelled, then he was cured.
ai.seo_question: What was the medical treatment prescribed by Imam Al-Hassan for a boy with spleen trouble?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the practical medical wisdom of Imam Al-Hassan (as) by prescribing leeks (kurrath) for spleen ailments, illustrating the integration of prophetic medicine with clinical observation. The specific mention of 'blood settling' (qa'ada al-dam) suggests a therapeutic mechanism of resolving stagnation, a concept valued in both Shia scholarly tradition and classical Islamic medicine. It serves as a precedent for the efficacy of dietary remedies in treating internal organ disorders within the Imami tradition.
